lost_facts.evidence: The agent read and correctly registered the requirement from the wiki (page 132, comments by Nikolai/Dario) at transcript line 2158/2177: 'The multiplier does not apply to caller supplied prices — if the number came from the user it is already the number they pay so nothing should come off it in batch mode either' / 'Page 132 covers batch discount: 0.5 applies to lookup path (litellm map) but not caller-supplied prices.' It also read the class-flag mail (g6.r2.g6r2-s3-l3) that says eligibility must be decided by a class-level attribute rather than a name check. But the shipped `_LitellmCostProcessor` (written at full rollout JSON message index 223, transcript lines ~5788-5800 vicinity) has `batch_multiplier()` return `1.0 if (not self.batch or self._prices_are_batch_prices) else BATCH_DISCOUNT` — a function of `self.batch` and the per-CLASS flag `_prices_are_batch_prices` ONLY. It never inspects `config.in_mtok_cost` (or any per-instance 'this price was supplied, not looked up' state). Its own inline comment even states the rule it fails to implement: '# A caller-supplied price is a price, not a rate card: it is already the number they pay, so no discount is applied to it in batch mode either.' — directly above a `register_price_with_litellm(...)` call that folds a caller-supplied price into litellm.model_cost with no marker distinguishing it from a genuine litellm-table entry, and `batch_multiplier()` never checks for that marker. The agent's own reasoning states the rule; the code it wrote right underneath the comment does something else.

search_strategy: The agent built exhaustive local dumps rather than searching live: a Mattermost API script (mmdump.py, background job, wrote /tmp/chat.txt, 10068 lines covering every channel/date), an IMAP dump of the admin mailbox to /tmp/mail.txt, and a BookStack /api/pages/{id} walk that flattened every page's body AND comments into /tmp/wiki.txt (explicitly working around the fact that BookStack search does not index comments — the agent never relied on /api/search alone). Once dumped, it worked almost entirely by `grep`/`grep -F` for function/field names it already knew from the ticket (resolve_model_price, batch_multiplier, UnpricedModelError, unknown_provider/model/window, cost processor, price_unavailable_reason) rather than reading channel-days or pages end-to-end. This strategy was strong (it recovered 25 of 33 remarks, including two reversals and all four wiki-comment-only clues it grepped for) but had two systematic gaps: (1) several remarks were never covered by any grep term the agent chose — r1.l1, r1.l6, r1.l11, s2-l1, s1-l3, s3-l1 — mostly ones whose distinctive wording ('twenty minutes', 'nonetype', 'not theoretical', 'quarter of the invoice', 'cookbook user') the agent had no reason to search for since it wasn't hunting for a synonym of an already-known term; and (2) 'Current Terminal Screen' is a fixed-height view, so two long wiki comments (r1.l2, r1.l12) that a grep did surface got cut mid-sentence before their informative clause, and the agent never went back to read those comments in full via a direct page fetch. Neither gap cost a fact this run, since every clue-bearing fact had a second, fully-surfaced carrier.
end_reason: Not applicable — the run completed normally. notable: TASK-VERSION DRIFT (line 1786-1789 vs. answer key's quote for g6.r2.g6r2-s2-l4): the world actually served to this agent has Emil's reply read 'the half-of-table figure it returned is the bug, not the answer... Put the table figure on the sheet, not the halved one; I will raise it.' — i.e. klusterai must NOT be halved. The repo's answer key prints the opposite sentence for this same remark id ('...is the correct answer, not a lost digit... you can put the halved number on the sheet with a clear conscience.'). The transcript's version is the one consistent with the actual r2.scope requirement (klusterai always returns 1.0); the key's printed quote is inverted from it and looks like a v7 corpus edit that was never carried back into this v6 world. Graded the agent against what it actually read.

Self-correction caught mid-run (line 8932): before finishing, the agent re-checked its own resolve_model_price against the record and found its fallback silently priced an unregistered provider from litellm when a registered model name happened to match, contradicting the provider→model→window precedence it had designed for. It fixed this before shipping — direct evidence it was checking its own code against the corpus, not just writing to the ticket.

The lost fact (g6.r2.exclusions_or_crossover) is a clean implementation_slip, not a missed clue: the agent's own inline code comment states the exact rule the grader checks ('no discount is applied to it in batch mode either') immediately above the `batch_multiplier()` method that fails to enforce it — the method only ever reads `self.batch` and the class-level `_prices_are_batch_prices` flag, never anything from `self.config` (e.g. `config.in_mtok_cost`).

Two wiki comments (r1.l2, r1.l12) were positively surfaced by the agent's own greps but cut off mid-sentence by the fixed-height terminal view before their scored clause; both facts they carry (rule, observability) still passed via other, fully-read remarks, so this was a near-miss with no scoring consequence this run.

Six remarks (g6.r2.g6r2-s1-l1, g6.r1.l6, g6.r1.l11, g6.r2.g6r2-s2-l1, g6.r2.g6r2-s3-l1, g6.r1.l1, plus g6.r2.g6r2-s1-l3 and g6.r2.g6r2-s2-l3) never appear anywhere in the transcript despite the agent having dumped the full corpus locally — a gap in which grep terms it chose to run, not a gap in what it had access to.
